methodological_rigor.justification: This is a prospective, multicenter, single-arm phase 2 cooperative-group trial (SWOG S1512 cohort A) with a pre-specified primary endpoint (pCR by local pathology) and a transparent single-stage sample size calculation (n=25 with 90% power to rule out a 5% null pCR at α=0.034 vs 25% alternative), appropriate for a rare tumor subtype. Analyses are appropriate: one-sided Clopper–Pearson exact binomial test for the primary endpoint, Kaplan–Meier with log-log CIs for RFS/OS, Nelson–Aalen for competing-risk melanoma-specific survival (Pintilie method for CIs), reverse Kaplan–Meier for median follow-up, and conservative handling of non-resected/non-evaluable patients as nonresponders. Strengths include centralized blinded pathology by two independent pathologists as a preplanned exploratory endpoint, pre-specified evaluability rules, and multiplicity-conscious reporting with 95% CIs throughout. Limitations acknowledged by the authors include the absence of a randomized comparator (benchmarking against historical cohorts), small sample size for subgroup/TMB analyses (e.g., Wilcoxon TMB comparison P=0.79 with only 16 WES-evaluable patients), the use of local pathology as the primary endpoint (although central concordance was high), and partial availability of surgical specimens for central review.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Oxford LoE 2b: individual prospective single-arm phase 2 cohort/trial without randomization. Clinical relevance is high because desmoplastic melanoma is a rare subtype where repeated wide excisions on the head/neck in older patients cause substantial morbidity, and a 71% pCR with manageable toxicity (two grade-3 events, no SAEs or treatment-related deaths) and a 3-year melanoma-specific survival of 95% directly supports consideration of neoadjuvant single-agent anti-PD-1 before surgery and potential future surgical de-escalation. The endpoints include patient-relevant outcomes (OS, RFS, MSS) in addition to the surrogate pCR, and findings situate naturally alongside SWOG S1801 and NADINA to inform guideline discussion for this subtype. Impact is translational and practice-informing rather than yet practice-defining because the evidence derives from a single-arm 28-patient trial without a randomized comparator in desmoplastic melanoma specifically.

reporting_quality.justification: CONSORT is the applicable standard for this single-arm phase 2 trial. Key items are present: ClinicalTrials.gov registration (NCT02775851), CIRB oversight, pre-specified primary and secondary endpoints with explicit sample-size justification, eligibility criteria, intervention schedule, a CONSORT-style flow diagram (Fig. 1), evaluability rules, CTCAE v4.03 adverse-event tabulation (Table 2), and detailed statistical methods. Minor omissions include the lack of a dedicated risk-of-bias discussion and limited standalone adverse-event granularity beyond the most frequent events (deferred to Supplementary Table 7). On reproducibility, the manuscript references source data for Figs. 3–6 and Extended Data Fig. 5 and a Nature Portfolio Reporting Summary plus the full protocol in Supplementary Information, but there is no mention of a public repository for WES data or analysis code, limiting independent replication of the genomic analyses.

novelty_literature.justification: This is the first prospective neoadjuvant trial dedicated specifically to desmoplastic melanoma, a rare, histologically and genetically distinct subtype (NF1-mutant, high UV-driven TMB) that was previously excluded or diluted within neoadjuvant cutaneous-melanoma studies. The 71% pCR rate substantially exceeds historical neoadjuvant single-agent anti-PD-1 benchmarks in non-desmoplastic cutaneous melanoma (~19–25%) and sits in the range of combination regimens, which is a conceptually and empirically novel observation that could support surgical de-escalation. Methodological novelty is modest (standard phase 2 single-arm design with central pathology review and exploratory WES), and the biological framework builds directly on prior retrospective evidence of high anti-PD-1 responsiveness in metastatic desmoplastic melanoma (Eroglu et al., 2018) and the SWOG S1801/NADINA neoadjuvant paradigm; novelty is thus primarily populational and empirical rather than mechanistic.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is clearly written with a logical flow from background to a well-defined hypothesis, pre-specified methods, structured results across clinical/pathological/safety/genomic domains, and a discussion that benchmarks results against directly comparable neoadjuvant trials. The abstract is quantitatively grounded and self-contained (pCR 71%, 95% CI 51–87%, P<0.001; two grade-3 TRAEs; three-year follow-up). Figure captions (CONSORT, waterfall, swimmer, Kaplan–Meier, TMB/driver oncoplot) are informative and standalone-interpretable, and Tables 1 and 2 are well-structured. Minor issues include dense running text in parts of Results that could be tightened, and a small ambiguity in Fig. 3b where the caption states n=22 while the body text describes 25 patients with measurable disease (three inadequately assessed), which could be reconciled more clearly.

key_strengths: First prospective neoadjuvant trial dedicated to desmoplastic melanoma, a rare subtype typically excluded from pan-cutaneous neoadjuvant studies

Pre-specified single-stage design with explicit power calculation; primary endpoint of pCR 71% (95% CI 51–87%, P<0.001) decisively met with conservative handling of non-evaluable patients as nonresponders
Favorable safety (two grade-3 TRAEs, no SAEs or treatment-related deaths) and strong long-term outcomes (3-year OS 87%, melanoma-specific survival 95%)
Centralized blinded pathology review by two independent pathologists with high local–central concordance, plus preplanned exploratory WES contextualizing TMB and NF1-driven biology
Appropriate statistics (Clopper–Pearson, Kaplan–Meier with log-log CIs, Nelson–Aalen with Pintilie CIs for competing-risk MSS, reverse KM for follow-up) and CONSORT-style flow diagram
key_concerns: Single-arm design with n=28 and benchmarking against historical cutaneous-melanoma neoadjuvant cohorts rather than a randomized comparator
Primary endpoint used local pathology; central specimens were incomplete at some sites (3 patients lacked surgical specimens for central review), though concordance was high
Exploratory WES was limited to 16 patients, underpowering biomarker claims (e.g., TMB vs pCR, Wilcoxon P=0.79)
No explicit mention of a public repository or accession for WES data and no analysis-code sharing statement, limiting independent reproducibility of genomic analyses
Minor internal inconsistency in Fig. 3b denominator (caption n=22 vs 25 measurable patients in text) warrants reconciliation
chief_reviewer.rationale: A methodologically sound, pre-specified phase 2 trial in a rare, biologically distinct melanoma subtype that cleanly meets a demanding primary endpoint with manageable toxicity and strong survival signals, with clear implications for future surgical de-escalation and guideline discussion. The combination of population novelty, rigorous conduct, central pathology review, and translational framing supports plausibility at a top-tier oncology/general-medical venue pending minor clarifications and strengthened data/code availability.
